A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CrossMPT by the same authors. All 13 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CrossMPT decoding simulations, training-time measurements and masking/convergence experiments in the main text and Appendices A-C.

after.justification: v2 retains original decoding results and reports additional baseline comparisons, channel experiments, attention analyses and efficiency measurements, including in its appendices.

M1.justification: The core decoder, alternating masked cross-attention updates, parameter sharing and ordinary training loss remain unchanged. However, v2 Appendix E actually applies denoising diffusion to CrossMPT; v1 Appendix C only suggested this extension. The additional architecture equations mainly document the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation from AWGN to Rayleigh fading on six codes and adds BCH (31,21), BCH (255,223) and LDPC (32,16) cases. The earlier long-code suite is retained in Appendix A. Several timing-only cases disappear, including WiMAX (576,432) and WRAN (384,288) and (384,192). The new channel conditions substantially broaden coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds ML decoding, SCL decoding with list sizes 1 and 4, and additionally masked ECCT as comparators. BP also joins the long-code performance comparison. Conversely, the unmasked CrossMPT control disappears. DDECC, also called DDECCT in v2, is the existing diffusion baseline, but its comparison contracts from 14 code cases to five.

E3.justification: v2 adds FLOPs, per-codeword inference-time and mask-density metrics, and BP iteration sweeps of 20, 50 and 100 in Figure 9. Its efficiency table uses N=6 throughout, replacing v1's mixed N=2,3,6 suite. The reported BER testing rule retains 500 frame errors but omits the former minimum of 100,000 random codewords; this does not establish that fewer samples were actually tested.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons of attention relationships, controlled single-bit-error and error-free attention visualizations, an ECCT masking ablation, and tests separating diffusion benefits from architecture benefits. These substantially expand the evidence about how CrossMPT works. However, v1 Appendix A's no-mask CrossMPT convergence control is removed from the retained analysis in v2 Appendix I.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. v2's attention averages across layers do not constitute new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 is numerically identical, and the earlier long-code curves are retained. v2 nevertheless adds extensive baseline, fading, ablation, diffusion and efficiency results. For WRAN (384,320), N=6 and d=32, ECCT/CrossMPT epoch times change from 246/86 seconds to 305/104 seconds. New Table 3 reports CrossMPT polar (128,86) scores of 7.86/11.45/15.47, conflicting with 7.51/10.83/15.24 retained in Tables 1 and 4.

T1.justification: The central complexity derivation is substantially revised. v1 Section 5.2 derives dense-attention operation counts and the rate-dependent ratio gamma=2(1-R)/(2-R)^2<1/2. v2 Section 6.4 replaces this analysis with complexity expressions including projection costs and mask densities, defining h, h1 and h2 and arguing h>h1+h2 using the density comparison. This changes the computational assumptions and quantitative reasoning.

C1.justification: The core architectural novelty and superior-decoding claims remain. v2 adds the prominent claim that CrossMPT approaches ML decoding on short codes and broadens the efficiency claims to memory usage, FLOPs and inference time. The abstract and conclusion shift from emphasizing a quantified attention-complexity reduction toward broader decoder efficiency and long-code applicability.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the attention and masking evidence as showing that magnitude-syndrome relationships are the crucial interactions, and interprets layerwise attention as tracking error correction. It adds explanations concerning specialized SCL decoding and gains complementary to diffusion. Appendix J introduces a conditional hardware-pipelining argument for comparable throughput; no measured throughput results accompany that argument.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents positional embedding equations, query/key/value construction and the zero versus negative-infinity masking convention for the existing architecture. It also specifies the Rayleigh fading distribution and scale parameter for the new experiment. Core optimizer, training budget, hardware and existing PCM/ECCT source information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds recent Choukroun and Wolf works on foundation models and joint code learning, explaining their different objectives and potential complementarity rather than evaluating them. It adds earlier model-free decoding and hardware-related references while pruning generic vision/NLP citations. The principal model-based/model-free positioning and architectural novelty claim remain intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, background and architecture explanations are extensively rewritten. Related Works moves from after the conclusion to Section 2, the discussion becomes a broader ablation-and-analysis section, and existing appendix material is redistributed among dedicated comparison and analysis sections. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and the architecture and mask diagrams are redesigned. Earlier long-code plots are merged into v2 Figure 8, the main BER figure is reduced from six panels to three, and Table 2 is rebuilt around multiple efficiency metrics. New heatmaps, comparison plots, tables and a pipeline diagram substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the paper's central claims through ML/SCL comparisons, attention and masking controls, Rayleigh-channel evaluation, diffusion compatibility tests, and FLOPs/inference-time reporting. These address important gaps in v1's evidence about competitiveness, mechanism and practical efficiency. Removing the no-mask control, narrowing diffusion comparisons and introducing the inconsistent Table 3 row weaken parts of the reporting, but the broader and more diagnostic evidence provides a clear net improvement.
